reports.title: Leonard Harmsworth: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Wales prevention of future deaths reports (2019 onwards)

concerns.quote: Following the fall at home on 7th June 2022 WAST were contacted at 05:23. An ambulance arrived 17 hours 22 minutes later. On arrival at Ysbyty Glan Clwyd Leonard Harmsworth then waited in the ambulance for 12 hours 4 minutes before being handed over to nursing staff.
I remain significantly concerned that delays are continuing and that deaths will continue to occur into the future.
I have previously issued Prevention of Future Death Reports to BCUHB and WAST pertaining to the length of time it is taking for ambulances to arrive to patients and handover at hospitals.
concerns.hazard: lack of action on previous reports

promises.quote: We have produced several guidelines to help clinicians treating children presenting with fever and symptoms such as those in the case of Sienna. These include; fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management [NG143], sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management [NG51] and sore throat (acute): antimicrobial prescribing [NG84].
promises.summary: Produced clinical guidelines for fever, sepsis, and sore throat management

links.explanation: Both reports identify ambulance handover delays at hospitals as the cause of delayed ambulance response to patients needing emergency care. The later report reiterates that these delays exceed national targets and affect response times.
links.earlier_quote: The delay in an ambulance being despatched to the home address of the deceased who was clearly experiencing seizures/fits. The evidence showed that the main reason for the delay was the significant hand over delays being experienced at the 2 district general hospitals
links.later_quote: As stated in his evidence at para 45, the handover delays experienced at/around the time that the deceased was awaiting assistance were well in excess of the targets enshrined in the Welsh Health Circular of May 2016.
links.promise_quote: We recognise lengthy handover delays are clearly unacceptable as they can impact not only on the ambulance service's ability to respond to subsequent calls in the community, but also on patient's experience. Handover delays are often symptomatic of pressures elsewhere within the unscheduled care system and should not be viewed in isolation which is why work is being undertaken nationally and locally to support improvements across the patient pathway through reducing inappropriate admissions to hospital
